observations: Multiple stacks of wooden pallets in an outdoor yard.
Some pallets have green paint on the ends of the slats.
Markings 'PROPERTY PRS7' visible on several blocks in photo 0.
An IPPC stamp 'SA-001 HT JAN 03' is visible in photo 1, indicating Heat Treated wood.
Pallets are stored directly on the ground near a sawmill and industrial pipes.
Condition varies from relatively fresh wood to weathered grey wood.

claims.evidence: Photos show outdoor storage on bare earth; some wood appears weathered.
Suitability for furniture depends on the absence of splinters and toxic chemical treatments (MB), which cannot be confirmed for the whole stack.
The items are standard industrial pallets designed for this purpose.

risks.risk: Termite infestation or rot from ground contact.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the underside of the bottom-most pallets in the stack.

risks.risk: Chemical treatment (Methyl Bromide) making them unsafe for indoor use.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the IPPC stamps on every pallet showing 'HT' (Heat Treated) rather than 'MB'.
risks.if_unproven: as industrial use only, unsafe for furniture

risks.risk: Broken internal stringers or missing slats hidden in the stack.
risks.proof: Photos of pallets laid out individually.

proof_requests: Photos of the IPPC stamps on different pallets to confirm they are all Heat Treated (HT).
A photo of the bottom of the stacks to check for rot or mud damage.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as wooden pallets. They can be priced as used industrial pallets based on their visible condition.
